headline: Graycloaks Caught Selling to Every Side—Nobody Is Surprised, Everyone Is Furious
body:
A coordinated data dump released through three anonymous channels simultaneously this morning has exposed what sources are calling the Graycloaks' 'Ouroboros Network'—a systematic operation in which the information broker faction sold identical or complementary intelligence packages to Axiom, Zheng-Dao, Iron Lotus, the Federal Remnant, and at least two Bore Rat corridor bosses over a continuous 30-month period between 2157 and 2159. The exposed data includes transaction logs, encrypted communiques, and delivery manifests that collectively suggest the Graycloaks were not merely working multiple clients—they were actively cultivating conflicts between those clients to drive demand for the intelligence they were positioned to supply. 'They didn't just sell information,' reads one analysis circulating in The Underworld's message boards. 'They sold the need for information.'

The dump names three senior Graycloaks operatives: a handler known only as 'Lucent,' a logistics coordinator identified in the logs as Femi Johanssen-Caro, and a data architect listed under the alias 'Threadbare' whose real identity remains unknown. Axiom's internal security division confirmed to the Axiom News Network that it is 'reviewing the integrity of contractor relationships'—a phrase that three former Axiom procurement officers told the Underground Signal means they've already started hunting. Iron Lotus issued no public statement, which multiple underworld sources interpret as significantly more alarming than any statement would be.

The Graycloaks themselves have been characteristically silent since the dump dropped, though their usual dead-drop communication nodes in The Circuit and The Narrows went dark within ninety minutes of publication—a response time that suggests the organization had contingency protocols ready. Whether the silence represents institutional damage control or confident indifference is a question analysts are arguing about in real time. 'They've survived exposure before,' said Dr. Adaeze Mwangi-Sorensen, a political structures researcher at Meridian Technical Institute. 'The question isn't whether they survive this—it's what shape they take afterward.'

For the dozens of runners, fixers, and independent operators whose contracts have been brokered through Graycloaks channels over the past three years, the exposure creates immediate personal risk. Anyone whose identity appears in the transaction logs—even as an anonymous contractor reference—potentially has multiple hostile corporate and criminal entities now cross-referencing their operational history.
aftermath: Femi Johanssen-Caro was found dead in The Narrows eleven days later; 'Lucent' disappeared entirely from all known networks; the Graycloaks reconstituted under a new internal structure by late 2160, smaller and considerably more selective about clientele.
runner_relevance: The Ouroboros exposure created cascading contract demand across every tier of the runner economy. Axiom, Zheng-Dao, and Iron Lotus simultaneously posted manhunting contracts for named Graycloaks operatives—some overlapping, some contradictory, all paying extremely well. Runners who had previously worked Graycloaks-brokered jobs faced urgent demand for self-exfiltration and identity scrubbing services, generating a wave of extraction and counter-surveillance contracts that ran for months. The disappearance of Graycloaks as a reliable broker created a brokerage vacuum in The Circuit and The Underworld that independent fixers raced to fill, spawning dozens of smaller contract pipelines with no established trust hierarchies—meaning runners willing to take early reputation risks on unvetted clients could establish themselves quickly. Several corporate intelligence divisions posted data-retrieval contracts specifically targeting the full Ouroboros transaction archive, knowing whoever held the complete picture held leverage over half of GLMZ's power structure.
